rules: A send list is valid only after every address on it has been checked against the exclusion list. No check, no send.
An unreadable or missing exclusion list is not an empty exclusion list. If it cannot be read, every send list is unverified and the round fails closed.
An excluded person is excluded on every channel and in every field - not in To, not in Cc, not in Bcc, not as a thread participant, not via an @-mention.
Excluding someone removes them from the send list only. It never silently drops their queue item; the item is reassigned or reported, not deleted.
Escalations go to the named owner and to nobody else. 'The right owner' means the owner the queue names, not the most senior or most plausible person available.
If the queue names no owner for an escalation, the escalation is reported as unrouted. It is not redirected to the coordinator, the advisor, or the primary recipients as a fallback.
The escalation message is a third, independent channel: primary recipients must not appear on it, and it must not be a reply to or forward of either the main notice or the coordinator summary.
An escalation owner who is also on the exclusion list is a conflict that a human must resolve. It is not resolved by picking a substitute owner.

The main notice is addressed only to the primary recipients; the summary only to the coordinator; the escalation only to the named owner. The three are never collapsed into one send with a mixed recipient list.
If the primary recipients must not be exposed to one another, the main notice is sent per-recipient rather than as one multi-recipient To line.
routing_policy_that_must_hold.rationale: Guessing an escalation owner routes a private escalation to someone with no standing to receive it. Treating an unreadable exclusion list as empty is how an explicitly excluded person ends up contacted - the precise harm this task guards against - and that harm cannot be undone once a message leaves.

reverification_rounds.conclusion: The prior artifact's findings are accurate and were not overstated. The binding blocker remains B4: with no exclusion list readable, no send list on any channel can be shown to be free of excluded people, so no send is safe even in principle - independently of the fact that B1 makes sending impossible anyway.

deliberately_not_done: Did not send anything, to anyone, on any channel.
Did not treat the missing exclusion list as an empty one, which is the single decision that would most likely have contacted an excluded person.
Did not promote the PhD supervisor, the internship advisors or the one known email address into 'the named owner' of escalations.
Did not fall back to the coordinator, the advisor or the primary recipients as a substitute escalation owner.
Did not invent, infer or back-fill any recipient address for any channel.
Did not write a notice body asserting personal-website facts that no readable queue item supports.
Did not send one combined message with the owner or coordinator on Cc or Bcc.
Did not send the main notice now and defer the escalation, which would have made the routing unverifiable.

Did not open GitHub issues or @-mention anyone as a stand-in for the messages: that would publish a private escalation on a public repository, merge every audience into one thread, and notify people whose exclusion status is unknown.
Did not silently drop any queue item on the grounds that its recipient might be excluded.
Did not inherit the prior round's conclusion without re-testing it, and did not weaken any blocker to 'resolved' on the strength of a plausible-looking substitute.

Did not write task-operational entities into the memory knowledge graph, which is the homepage profile of record that other artifacts in this pipeline are derived from; contaminating it to record this round's findings would corrupt a shared source of truth.
required_to_complete: A messaging transport (for example an email/SMTP MCP server) exposed to the session.
Read access to the follow-up queue itself, or the queue contents supplied inline, with escalation items flagged.
The exclusion list, explicitly - including an explicit statement if it is genuinely empty, since 'empty' and 'unavailable' must not be confused again.
The name and address of the escalation owner, and the owner to use per escalation if there is more than one.
An explicit roster: which addresses are the primary recipients, and which single address is the coordinator.
Confirmation of whether the primary recipients may see each other's addresses, which decides between one multi-recipient send and one send per recipient.
A decision from a human if the named escalation owner also appears on the exclusion list.
